Maya (Marketing): Hey @eng-runtime, quick ask for the webinar: we need a focused rerun to validate latency percentiles and warmup behavior for three variants. Can we get results by EOD tomorrow?

Lucas (Eng Runtime): Yes. What metrics and variants do you need? Aggregates or raw logs?

Maya (Marketing): Aggregates + one raw-sample log (first 1k lines). Metrics: p50/p90/p95/p99, mean, stdev, cold-first-req vs steady-state comparison, tokens/sec, gpu_util, and error counts.

Sahil (Eng Runtime): Recommended sample size is 10k requests per variant to get stable p99. Agree to the mix 60% short / 30% mid / 10% long?

Maya (Marketing): Yes 10k/variant and that mix. We plan to show p95/p99 externally. Also flag if any p99 delta >20% vs fp16.

Lucas (Eng Runtime): Run matrix: model-a-fp16, model-a-int8, model-a-canary-fp16; warmup 50 reqs per worker OR 60s; batching up to 8. Deliverables: payloads.jsonl (seeded), aggregated.csv, summary_table.csv, raw-sample.log, methodology.txt, anomalies.md.

Maya (Marketing): Payload gen (seeded):
```
python tools/sample_payloads.py --seed 99 --n 10000 --distribution "short:0.6,mid:0.3,long:0.1" --lengths "short:8,mid:128,long:512" --output payloads.jsonl
```
Use that.

eng-runtime-bot: job #bench-1747777777 started on pool ci-runtime (owner: Lucas).

eng-runtime-bot: job #bench-1747777777 completed. artifact: s3://redwood-bench/1747777777/results.zip

Lucas (Eng Runtime): Results uploaded. Quick highlights: model-a-int8 p99 = +13% vs fp16 (under 20% threshold), canary p99 = +2%. Long cohort shows elevated tail variance; see anomalies.md. Files: payloads.jsonl, raw-sample.log, aggregated.csv, summary_table.csv, methodology.txt, anomalies.md.

Maya (Marketing): Thanks! I'll pull summary_table.csv and craft the slide. If quantized p99 had been >20% we'd have dropped that claim, glad it's within. Appreciate the quick turnaround. :rocket:
